Cross-tissue senescence hub-gene study in type 2 diabetes: results report

Computational study, human GEO microarray data; assembled from saved results only

Summary

  • Islet arm. Nested-CV AUC 0.659 (95% CI 0.528-0.789, sample-level bootstrap). The apparent AUC of the full-cohort model on its own training data is 0.766 and is optimistic. The final panel is a single gene, IL1R1. On independent islets (GSE76894, n = 99) the frozen model gives AUC 0.591 (0.435-0.738): the interval includes 0.5, so the discovery signal is not demonstrated to replicate. The secondary islet set (GSE20966, n = 20) gives 0.560 (0.290-0.820), also including 0.5.
  • Adipose arm. Nested-CV AUC 0.532 (0.384-0.682): indistinguishable from chance. The apparent AUC is 0.871. The final panel is a single gene, SNAI1. External validation (GSE71416, n = 17) gives AUC 0.439 (0.136-0.742), and the direction of effect is opposite to discovery in both adipose validation sets. The adipose result is a null result.
  • Of the four headline numbers, 1 of 4 has a confidence interval that excludes 0.5 (islet nested CV).
  • Cross-tissue. No shared gene between the two panels; the overlap is not a finding (primary permutation p = 1.000, which is 1 by construction when the observed overlap is 0).
  • Docking was not performed: under protocol 5.4 the only candidate (IL1R1, stability 0.42) fails criterion (a), stability >= 0.5.
  • Sensitivity analyses show the panels are unstable. The islet AUC rises when 11 label-discordant donors are removed, but that is a hypothesis, not a finding.

1. Study design and data

Two parallel arms (islet, adipose): discovery, then a nested-CV-validated hub-gene panel (senescence gene union screened by limma, then LASSO, SVM-RFE and Boruta/Random Forest, intersected, then a ridge classifier), then a single frozen-model pass on external cohorts. Followed by cross-tissue comparison, enrichment, single-cell specificity (islet only) and a docking target rule. Specification: docs/Methodology_Protocol_v1.md (v1.2). Human microarray data from NCBI GEO; no wet-lab component.

Notes on group definitions and data handling. GSE27951: group from the GEO clinical status field (NGT = ND, DM = T2D, IGT excluded); three samples (GSM691135, GSM691139, GSM691140) have title/field discordance, the field is used, and a sensitivity rerun covers the PCA outlier (section 4). GSE71416: group from sample titles (no disease field in GEO). GSE41762: all 77 arrays normalised together; the submitters’ donor 1-48 / 49-80 split is carried as the covariate submitter_norm_batch. Each GSE is normalised independently; no cross-cohort batch correction anywhere.

GSE38642 retirement. Task 2 showed that all 63 of its CEL files are byte-identical (decompressed MD5) to arrays of GSE41762, so it provides no independent data. 11 donors carry a different diabetes label in GSE38642 than in GSE41762 (10 ND in GSE38642 but T2D in GSE41762; 1 the reverse). That discordance is handled as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis (section 4) and is also a limitation (section 9).

2. Headline results

The four numbers. Nested-CV AUC is honest and is the headline (CLAUDE.md rule 5); the apparent AUC (full-cohort model scored on its own training data) is optimistic and appears only beside it. Two 95% CIs per number: headline = sample-level stratified bootstrap (2000 replicates); protocol = pROC::ci.auc (2000 stratified bootstraps). For the discovery arms the protocol CI is computed on pooled out-of-fold predictions of all repeats and is too narrow (the repeats are not independent); the headline interval is the more conservative one (logs/deviations.md, 2026-10-05). For the external cohorts there is one prediction per sample, so the two intervals come out identical in the saved file.

Plain reading.

  • Islet. Nested-CV AUC 0.659 (0.528-0.789) is above chance under both interval methods, and is well below the apparent AUC of 0.766. The panel is one gene (IL1R1), selected in only 0.42 of outer folds. External AUC is 0.591 in GSE76894 (0.435-0.738) and 0.560 in GSE20966 (0.290-0.820). The sign of the effect matches discovery in both, but both intervals include 0.5. The most the data support is a weak, unreplicated islet signal.
  • Adipose. Nested-CV AUC 0.532 with an interval centred on 0.5 under both methods; the apparent AUC of 0.871 is overfitting of a one-gene model on 23 samples. External AUC 0.439 (0.136-0.742) is below 0.5 and the direction of the gene is opposite to discovery in GSE71416 and GSE16415. There is no adipose result.

3. Leakage controls

Three controls were run on the discovery arms before any validation data were touched (protocol section 3 self-tests): no sample index in both train and test of a fold; the matrix passed to limma in each fold has exactly the training-fold size (both are hard assertions in scripts/06_nested_cv.R); a label-permutation test of the full pipeline; plus a synthetic positive control.

3.1 Permutation tests

Permutation test: 20 independent label shuffles, full pipeline, 1 outer repeat each (summarised from the saved per-shuffle AUCs).
Arm Shuffles Mean AUC SD Min 95th percentile Max Pass (mean in [0.45, 0.55] and 95th pct < 0.65)
Islet (GSE41762) 20 0.495 0.082 0.362 0.614 0.670 pass
Adipose (GSE27951) 20 0.477 0.136 0.250 0.642 0.742 pass

Both arms pass the pre-set criterion, so the nested-CV engine shows no sign of leakage. The adipose 95th percentile (0.642) is close to the 0.65 limit; with 23 samples the null distribution of AUC is wide (individual shuffles reach 0.742), which is a further reason the adipose AUC of 0.532 carries no information.

3.2 Synthetic positive control (islet engine)

Design (as logged in logs/06_nested_cv_20261005_212648.log, fixed before running): 3000 genes, 77 samples with the real ND/T2D labels, 10 randomly chosen senescence-union genes shifted by +1.5 SD in T2D, everything else noise, covariates independent of status; production pipeline, 10-fold x 2 repeats. Pre-stated pass: nested AUC >= 0.90 and >= 8 of the top-10 stability genes planted.

Result: nested-CV AUC 0.984 (protocol CI 0.968-0.995; sample-level CI 0.962-0.997); 9 of 10 planted genes are in the top 10 by stability; pass flag in the saved object: PASS. The pipeline therefore recovers a real signal when one exists. One planted gene (KDR) was not recovered (frequency 0.00).

3.3 Boruta warning diagnosis

During the Task 5 islet run Boruta 10.0.0 (default fru importance backend) emitted “getImp result contains NA(s)” in 47 of 50 folds. Diagnosis as logged in logs/deviations.md (2026-10-05; evidence in results/stage3/diagnostics/): NaN occurs only in the first ~15 of 499 iterations and is replaced by 0, so it cannot create a false confirmation. The production backend was kept for both arms, and a robustness check swapping in ranger importance gave the same final panel, the same top-3 stability genes and a nested AUC of 0.662 versus 0.659. This was a benign warning, reported, not a defect that changes any result.

Plain reading.

  • Adipose: not robust. Dropping one sample (GSM691134) changes the final panel completely (no shared gene), moves the nested AUC from 0.532 to 0.416 (below 0.5; interval 0.269-0.564), and the apparent AUC rises to 0.950 with an eight-gene panel. Adding BMI keeps the panel gene but leaves the AUC at chance (0.511). The adipose arm has no stable result.
  • Islet: the +BMI run is stable, the excl-11 run is a hypothesis. Adding BMI leaves nested AUC essentially unchanged (0.666 vs 0.659); the panel grows to five genes and retains IL1R1. Excluding the 11 label-discordant donors raises the nested AUC to 0.788 (0.686-0.880), but the panel changes entirely (SERPINE2, PCGF2, CD55, SFRP1; no gene shared with the main panel), the run has only 10 T2D donors, and 10 of the 11 excluded donors are labelled T2D in GSE41762 (so excluding them removes half of that cohort’s 20 T2D labels). The gain could reflect cleaner labels, a smaller and different cohort, or chance. It is a hypothesis, not a finding. It was a pre-specified descriptive run; it informed no decision and the headline stays on the main run.
  • Across runs the panels are single genes or small sets that do not carry over; the more reproducible quantity is the stability ranking (section 5), and even that moves between runs.

5.1 Islet WGCNA (GSE41762, n = 77)

Soft threshold beta = 13 (first beta in 1-20 with signed scale-free R^2 >= 0.85; R^2 = 0.858). 16 modules; 1 kept (abs(r) > 0.3 and p < 0.05 against status); 2 hubs (kME > 0.8, abs(GS) > 0.2, and a senescence-union DEG).

GPC3 lightcyan 0.878 0.411 2.04e-04 0.626 0.046 yes (BMI)

Hubs are GPC3 and FGF2. The kept module’s eigengene is also correlated with BMI (p = 0.043), so it is flagged as possibly BMI-confounded. IL1R1, the nested-CV panel gene, is not in any module (assigned to the grey/unassigned set, label 0; MAD rank 1088 of the full matrix, so it was eligible; kME and hub status not defined; gene significance for status 0.432, p = 8.87e-05). The WGCNA hubs and the ML panel therefore do not coincide. GPC3 and FGF2 had nested-CV stability of 0.02 and 0.02 respectively (islet).

5.2 Adipose WGCNA: stopped by the pre-set rule (GSE27951, n = 23)

The adipose WGCNA was stopped. No soft threshold in 1-20 reached scale-free R^2 >= 0.85; the best was R^2 = 0.764 at beta = 20 (n = 23). Per protocol 4.1 the curve is reported, no beta was chosen, and no modules, trait analysis or bootstrap stability analysis were run. The threshold was not lowered. WGCNA is reported as not feasible at this sample size; the adipose arm is described by the nested-CV result alone. Verdict text from 07_verdicts.csv: “ADIPOSE ARM STOPPED at the soft-threshold step (STOP: no beta in 1..20 reaches scale-free R^2 >= 0.85 (signed R^2); best = 0.764 at beta = 20. Curve saved; NO beta chosen; no modules, no trait analysis, no stability run.) Stability analysis (100 bootstraps) and adipose module-trait analysis NOT run; adipose WGCNA therefore yields no modules and is not reported (protocol §4.1: never pick a beta silently).”

6. Cross-tissue comparison and enrichment

6.1 Cross-tissue verdict

Cross-tissue comparison (10_overlap_summary.csv).
Item Value

Adipose final panel SNAI1

Hypergeometric universe size N 931
SECONDARY hypergeometric p (final panels) 1
Overlap of stability lists (freq >= 0.2), descriptive 0

Verdict (verbatim from the saved file):

NO OVERLAP: the islet final panel (IL1R1) and the adipose final panel (SNAI1) share no gene, and the screen+LASSO selections share no gene (observed overlap 0; primary permutation p = 1.0000, which equals 1 by construction when the observed overlap is 0; hypergeometric on the final panels p = 1). No cross-tissue overlap is reported as a finding; no shared hub-gene is claimed.

Degenerate-permutation caveat. The observed overlap is 0, so every one of the 1000 permutations satisfies null >= observed and the primary p equals 1 by construction; the test cannot discriminate in this situation. What it can show is the null itself: the overlap was 0 in 991 of 1000 permutations and 1 in 9 (never larger), so even a single shared gene would have had an empirical p of roughly 0.010. The same applies to the hypergeometric test (p = 1 for an overlap of 0). Neither test supports, or could have supported, a claim of shared hub genes here. Stated plainly: there is no cross-tissue overlap, and nothing is reported as a shared hub gene.

The shared set is empty and the islet-specific and adipose-specific sets each contain one gene (IL1R1 and SNAI1), so enrichment testing is underpowered and was not performed (protocol 5.2). Gene-level annotation only: IL1R1 (interleukin 1 receptor type 1) is annotated to cytokine/NF-kB and MAPK signalling and is in CellAge; it is a descriptive DEG in islets (BH p 0.017) but not in adipose. SNAI1 (snail family transcriptional repressor 1) is a transcriptional repressor annotated to adherens-junction biology and is in CellAge; it is not a descriptive DEG in adipose (no adipose gene passes FDR < 0.05). Both genes are single entries in one senescence database (CellAge) and their annotation is not evidence that they are mechanistic drivers.

E1 is exploratory and hypothesis-generating only. The 11 genes were chosen from the senescence union, so with the whole expressed genome as universe (background A) enrichment for growth-factor and development terms is inflated by that pre-selection; background B (senescence-union genes expressed in islets) removes that bias and is the appropriate one, and it still yields 45 terms across the four databases (versus 258 under A). With 11 genes, few of which are independent (the same handful of FGF/GPC3/HGF/MYC genes recur across terms), these counts should not be read as pathway discoveries. E2/E3 (islet stability list, freq >= 0.2: 9 genes; adipose: 2 genes; adipose DEGs: 0) were also below 10 genes and not tested.

Reading: no gene is shown to be beta-cell restricted; every verdict is inconclusive or not assessable. No gene reaches FDR < 0.05 in beta pseudobulk (smallest BH value 0.836), and the approximate minimum detectable effects in beta cells range from 0.10 to 1.85 log2 units across the panel genes (80% power, 6 ND vs 5 T2D donors), so absence of significance is not evidence of no effect. Because delta cells have no testable donors, the delta arm of the restriction rule cannot be assessed at all, so no gene could be declared fully beta-restricted even in principle. SNAI1 is detected in only 0.012 of beta cells and GPC3 is not fitted in beta or alpha (pseudobulk non-zero in fewer than 3 donors). IL1R1 is detected in 0.15 of beta cells and 0.31 of alpha cells, i.e. it is not beta-specific in expression.

Deviations affecting this section (full wording in section 10): GSE81608 on GEO has only an RPKM matrix, so pseudobulk is the mean of log2(RPKM+1) per donor and cell type tested with limma (no voom/edgeR on counts), which is less well calibrated than count-based pseudobulk; and the >= 10 cell threshold was not relaxed, so delta and PP pseudobulk tests were not performed.

8. Docking

Docking was NOT performed. Under protocol 5.4 the candidate set is the shared panel genes and, when there are none, the islet final panel. There are no shared genes (section 6), so the only candidate is IL1R1, with nested-CV selection frequency 0.42. Criterion (a) requires frequency >= 50%, so IL1R1 fails (a) and, per 5.4 item 4, “docking is reported as not performed under the rule. The rule is not relaxed.” The structure criterion (c) was not assessed, because (a) already excludes the candidate. No docking results exist and none are shown here. (Criterion (b) was amended in protocol v1.2 to information only; the direction in validation was concordant in both islet cohorts, but that is not a selection criterion.)

Ligand files were acquired from PubChem and are in ligands/ (embelin_CID3218_3D.sdf, embelin_CID3218_smiles.csv, LSC_NEEDED_FROM_LAB.md, naringenin_CID932_3D.sdf, naringenin_CID932_smiles.csv, rutin_CID5280805_3D.sdf, rutin_CID5280805_smiles.csv, SOURCES.md): naringenin (CID 932), embelin (CID 3218), rutin (CID 5280805). The lead small compound (LSC) structure is still needed from the lab (ligands/LSC_NEEDED_FROM_LAB.md); it has not been guessed or substituted.

Any docking performed later would be exploratory and could not be presented as following from the pre-specified rule. The only genes with stability >= 0.5 are SERPINE2 and NLK (islet; stability 0.70 and 0.52), and neither is in the final panel. If docking is run on them it must be labelled as outside protocol 5.4, with the controls of protocol 6.4 (redocking RMSD < 2 A; 40 property-matched decoys per ligand; delta-G reported as a decoy percentile). A docking score would predict binding geometry, not affinity or biological effect.

9. Limitations

Stated without softening.

  1. Adipose discovery n = 23 (11 ND / 12 T2D) is underpowered. It is too small for WGCNA (the arm stopped: no soft threshold reached R^2 >= 0.85) and too small for a stable ML panel (the panel changed completely when one sample was dropped). The adipose validation cohort GSE71416 was reduced by NUSE exclusion to n = 17 (6 ND / 11 T2D); its interval spans most of the AUC range.
  2. The validation cohorts are small and the intervals are wide. GSE20966 (n = 20), GSE71416 (n = 17) and GSE16415 (n = 10) are tiny; GSE76894 (n = 99, 19 T2D) is larger but its interval (0.435-0.738) still includes 0.5. None of the external AUCs is distinguishable from chance.
  3. GSE38642 is the same set of arrays as GSE41762 (63/63 CEL files byte-identical) and was retired; it provides no independent validation. 11 donors have discordant diabetes labels between the two GEO deposits (10 of them are T2D in GSE41762, i.e. half of that cohort’s T2D labels), and donor ID30 has a discordant sex. Which deposit is correct is unknown. GSE41762 labels were used for the main analysis.
  4. Bulk adipose cannot resolve the driving cell type. Adipose tissue is a mixture of adipocytes, stromal and immune cells; a gene-level signal in bulk may reflect composition differences. No adipose single-cell data were analysed.
  5. Cross-platform transfer attenuates the islet validation. The islet model was trained on GPL6244 (HuGene 1.0 ST) and applied to GPL570 (GSE76894) and GPL1352 (GSE20966) after z-scoring within each cohort; probe-set coverage, dynamic range and platform effects can reduce discriminative performance independently of biology, so a weaker external AUC is expected even for a real signal.
  6. Docking, if ever done, predicts geometry, not affinity. It was not done here (section 8).
  7. All data are cross-sectional. No causal or temporal inference is possible; senescence markers could be cause, consequence, or correlate of T2D, of treatment, or of obesity.
  8. Single-gene panels are unstable. Both final panels are one gene (IL1R1, SNAI1), selected in 42% and 46% of outer folds respectively; sensitivity runs produced different panels with no shared gene in two of four comparisons (section 4). A one-gene ridge classifier is a univariate marker, not a multi-gene signature.
  9. GSE81608 has only RPKM values and few T2D donors (5 to 6 per testable cell type); delta and PP cells are untestable. Pseudobulk on mean log RPKM is less calibrated than count pseudobulk.
  10. A vacuous assertion was left in scripts/09_external_validation.R (... | TRUE, which always passes). Editing the script after scoring would have changed its MD5 against the validation lock, so it was left in place. The other assertions are real and the dry run reproduced the stored apparent AUCs exactly (logs/deviations.md, 2026-10-06).
  11. SenMayo is 124 genes, not 125. The paper’s 125-gene list (Saul 2022, Supplementary Data 1) was not retrievable; the MSigDB 124-gene copy was used and the discrepancy is unresolved (recorded in logs/05_genesets_20261005_211636.log; the saved gene-set summary shows 124 SenMayo symbols).
  12. Sex calls are XIST-free for GSE41762 and GSE16415 (no XIST probe on those annotations; Y-gene mean only; deviation logged). GSE27951 has no recorded sex in GEO, so its sex covariate is expression-inferred. Two recorded-versus-inferred mismatches (GSE41762 ID30, GSE20966 GSM524170) were kept using the inferred value.
  13. Multiple analyses on small cohorts. The sensitivity runs and the exploratory analyses (E1, E2, E3, the 11-donor exclusion) are descriptive, and none of them should be quoted as a finding.

11. Reproducibility

  • renv.lock: R 4.5.2; Bioconductor 3.22; 245 packages (50 from Bioconductor). Lock taken on first run and not updated mid-project (CLAUDE.md). CLAUDE.md requires R >= 4.4 and Bioconductor >= 3.20; the lock satisfies both.
  • Seed policy (CLAUDE.md): every script calls set.seed(42) before any stochastic step; per-fold seeds in the nested-CV engine derive deterministically from 42 (fold-specific offsets); permutation shuffles use fixed offsets (4200 + i; see scripts). The scan below checks each script for a seed-42 call; 00_install.R is the package installer and has no stochastic step.

  • Dependency on rendering: Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("scripts/15_report.Rmd", output_dir = "results/report")' from the repository root with R_LIBS_USER=~/R/lib; it reads saved results and recomputes nothing. The render log is logs/15_report_<timestamp>.log.
  • Validation lock: results/stage5/09_VALIDATION_SCORED.lock records MD5s of the frozen models, scripts and result tables; the scoring script refuses to run again (log logs/09_external_validation_20261006_000131.log).

Appendix: data consistency checks performed while assembling this report

Cross-file consistency checks (a value read from two different saved files must agree). ‘MISMATCH’ rows would be flagged in the final hand-off.
check result detail
final n (pheno) equals n scored in 09 for each validation cohort consistent GSE76894, GSE20966, GSE71416, GSE16415
final n_T2D (pheno) equals n_T2D scored in 09 consistent
discovery n (pheno) equals n in 08 final panels consistent
permutation mean AUC (CSV) equals 08 permutation_mean_auc consistent islet and adipose; per-shuffle AUCs are rounded to 4 dp in the CSV
permutation 95th pct (CSV) equals 08 permutation_q95_auc consistent
08 sensitivity nested AUC equals 06b_sensitivity_comparison sens_nested_auc consistent
08 islet/adipose main nested AUC equals main_nested_auc in 06b_sensitivity_comparison consistent
08 panel-gene stability equals stability_selection tables consistent
10 final panels equal 08 final panels consistent
10 stability freq of final panel genes equals stability tables consistent

Observations not resolved by any check, recorded for the reader:

  • docs/Methodology_Protocol_v1.md section 1 lists GSE76894 as n = 103 (84 ND / 19 T2D) and GSE71416 as n = 20; the analysed sizes are 99 (80 / 19) and 17 (6 / 11) after the logged exclusions (table in section 1). This is expected, not an error.
  • The headline CI and the pROC CI are the same numbers for each external cohort in 09_validation_results.csv (one prediction per sample; the headline sample-level bootstrap and pROC::ci.auc stratified bootstrap coincide). They are shown in both columns for rule 6 and are not two independent estimates.
  • IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Task 11 text predates the amendments: it asks for a docking table with percentiles (docking not performed), describes GSE38642 as sharing donors with GSE41762 (the arrays are byte-identical), and lists GSE20966 as the primary islet validation (GSE76894 is primary since protocol v1.1). The report follows the protocol and CLAUDE.md.
